published.citation: Christiansen et al. 2010, dayside brightness temperature at 8 µm (NASA Exoplanet Archive emission table): 3100 +/- 240 K, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2010ApJ...710...97C/abstract

temperature.note: Its day side's brightness temperature is measured in secondary eclipse at 8 µm (Spitzer Space Telescope satellite Infrared Array Camera (IRAC)) and nobody has imaged it, so the color is a Planck spectrum at its published temperature.
temperature.chosen: 4 measured of 4 rows; the smallest relative uncertainty, then the longest wavelength
temperature.facility: Spitzer Space Telescope satellite Infrared Array Camera (IRAC)
